issue: All foreign keys fully covered; users<->experiment is 1:1
resolution: No action needed - referential integrity is clean

issue: avg_word_count and quality_answer_rate are NA whenever num_questions_asked == 0
resolution: NA is the mathematically correct value (mean of zero questions is undefined). Not imputed with 0, since 0 would misleadingly imply 'asked short questions'. Kept as NA; downstream analyses must use an explicit engaged-user flag.

issue: No full-row or primary-key duplicates found in any table
country & device_type in experiment.csv are 100% consistent (redundant) with users.csv
resolution: Redundant columns dropped from experiment_clean to avoid duplication; users.csv treated as source of truth

issue: num_questions_asked / avg_word_count / quality_answer_rate in experiment.csv are CUMULATIVE, ALL-TIME user stats (100% match to lifetime question counts), NOT stats measured after assignment_date (only 90.4% match). Using these columns directly for A/B comparison would conflate pre-existing user behavior with the treatment effect.
severity: high - methodological risk for causal inference
resolution: Engineered new post-assignment-only outcome metrics directly from questions.csv (num_questions_post, avg_word_count_post, quality_answer_rate_post) for valid A/B analysis; retained original all-time columns separately and clearly relabeled.

issue: questions.csv summary counters (num_views, num_answers, num_upvotes) do not fully reconcile with raw event counts in user_activity.csv (answers match 31.9%, upvotes 14.6%, views 0%).
severity: medium - treat as two independent measurement systems
resolution: Both sources kept as-is (no forced reconciliation). questions.csv treated as the authoritative snapshot/aggregate table; user_activity.csv treated as a separate behavioral event log best suited for sequencing/funnel/time-to-event analysis rather than as a re-derivation source for questions.csv's counters.

issue: All date columns parse cleanly as ISO dates with no out-of-range or malformed values
resolution: No cleaning required beyond type casting (done in Section 12)

issue: Right-skewed count/engagement distributions produce IQR-flagged 'outliers' in word_count (3.92%), num_upvotes (1.18%), and num_questions_asked (5.2%). These look like genuine highly-engaged users/popular questions rather than data errors (no negative values, no impossible magnitudes, e.g. max word_count = 275 words is a plausible long question).
severity: low - natural skew, not an error
resolution: Not removed or capped (task requires avoiding unnecessary deletion). Flag columns (e.g. is_word_count_outlier) added to the analytical dataset so downstream models can choose to winsorize/transform (e.g. log) if needed.
